overview.overview:
North Carolina remains one of the closest battlegrounds on the map, with 16 electoral votes that have repeatedly decided by single digits. The state voted Republican in 2020 by 1.3 points and again in 2024 by 3.2 points, running a few points to the right of the nation in both cycles. With the national environment favoring Democrats by roughly five points, the expected margin here is a narrow 2.2-point Democratic edge.

The state's lean of about 2.8 points Republican relative to the country means a strong national year is required for Democrats to carry it, while Republicans can win it even in a modestly favorable national climate. The 80 percent range spans from a 7-point Republican win to an 11-point Democratic win, reflecting genuine two-sided uncertainty.
overview.watch: Whether the national environment shifts toward Republicans, since even a few points of movement would flip North Carolina's expected margin back to the GOP.
key_factors: North Carolina's consistent Republican lean of about 2.8 points versus the nation offsets a favorable Democratic national environment
The state's recent margins (R+1.3 in 2020, R+3.2 in 2024) show it trending slightly away from Democrats even as it stays competitive
A roughly 5-point Democratic national environment would need to hold for the expected narrow Democratic edge to materialize
